A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TIGER and EchoSet. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching v1's visualization appendix H to v2's appendix I.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech-separation experiments, real-world evaluations, efficiency measurements, ablations and cinematic sound-separation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds an EchoSet comparison between TIGER (tiny) and SudoRM-RF + GC3 in Table 12.

M1.justification: The described modules and objectives are retained; TIGER (tiny) changes model sizes. However, Figure 2 moves the shared-input residual sum from the recurrent block's entrance to each unrolled block's output, including the final output. The PDFs do not explain whether this is a schematic correction or a computational change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate EchoSet, Libri2Mix, LRS2-2Mix, recorded real-world audio and DnR cinematic sound separation. The tiny-model experiment uses existing EchoSet coverage. Additional dataset and recording specifications do not establish new datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Appendix H and Table 12 add SudoRM-RF compressed using GC3 as a comparator for TIGER (tiny), distinct from the existing SudoRM-RF1.0x baseline. Comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: The new tiny-model experiment uses N=24 and H=64, versus N=128 and H=256 for TIGER (small), retaining B=4. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. Newly documented real-world recording and sliding-window settings do not establish that earlier evaluations were revised or rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix H investigates performance and efficiency at substantially smaller model capacity through TIGER (tiny). Existing band-split, module-removal, replacement and time-frequency-interleaving ablations remain, as do the four spectrogram case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain Appendix C's averaging over 1,000 timing passes. The new comparison follows the existing single-value reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 12 reports SI-SDRi of 10.4 dB for TIGER (tiny) versus 4.6 dB for SudoRM-RF + GC3, with 102.12K versus 303.57K parameters. Figure 4 removes the real-world SDRi results while retaining the scale-invariant scores. Existing numerical tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain their mathematical substance. Expanded explanation of the selective-attention equation and revised tensor notation do not introduce new derivations, formal assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's claim of being the first sub-million-parameter model with SOTA-comparable performance and Section 6.2's broader first-sub-million-model assertion. The TIGER/EchoSet contributions and principal performance and efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly justifies mixing separately recorded sources through independent sound propagation. Appendix C explains training-length-matched inference windows as protection against length mismatch and unfair comparisons. These add substantive methodological rationale without substantially revising the existing interpretations.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code release; v2 supplies code and EchoSet access links. It also documents recording hardware, microphone placement, distances, bit depth, clip duration, real-world sliding-window inference and tiny-model settings. Together these substantially expand reproducibility information; the linked resources were not externally verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Luo, Han and Mesgarani's GC3 work and explicitly compares against its compression approach. Removing the first-sub-million-model assertions narrows novelty positioning. The remaining cited literature and broad research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the introduction and related work, expands selective-attention and experimental explanations, updates publication and author information, and adds acknowledgments. Appendix H is inserted and visualization becomes Appendix I, while the overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a two-panel separator diagram. Figure 4 changes from two line plots to grouped bars, drops SDRi and relabels the retained metric from SI-SNRi to SI-SDRi. Table 1 is enlarged, Table 12 is added, and several existing displays are repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through detailed recording and inference documentation and resource-access information, adds a focused low-capacity comparison, and tempers priority claims. These gains are limited by unchanged principal experimental evidence, removal of real-world SDRi results and the unexplained residual-wiring difference in Figure 2.
